To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transport approach provides an unified picture of the build up of anisotropic flows, and that a study of the elliptic and triangular flow in the intermediate pT region allows to understand the different collective behavior observed at RHIC and LHC.

1) a transport approach to elliptic flow at fixed η/s is able to reproduce the experimental data in the intermediate momentum region; 2) a transport approach is also able to describe the pT dependence of v2 in the high momentum region and the saturation of the vT(pT) at LHC; 3) the rise and fall of v2 at LHC is related to the temperature dependence of the shear viscosity to entropy density ratio.
a microscopic description of anisotropic flows in heavy ion collisions can provide a tool to understand the transition from hydrodynamic regime to the high pT regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transport properties of strongly interacting matter in a wide range of temperatures.
the development of a new transport approach for relativistic heavy ion collisions, which includes the full set of equations of relativistic fluid dynamics.
a systematic study of the build up of elliptic flow in heavy ion collisions, with a special focus on the interplay of the hydrodynamic regime with the transport regime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrodynamics is a very useful tool, but not the only one, to study the collective flows.
the transport approach, in the context of the hydro regime, is a very powerful tool to study the build up of collective phenomena.
the transport approach provides an excellent tool to describe the build up of elliptic flow in a wide p_T range and for a broad range of viscosities, from the hydrodynamic regime to the kinetic one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transport approach, which has been used for many years to study the early time evolution of the QGP, is able to provide a good description of the elliptic flows at RHIC and LHC, in particular in the intermediate pT range where hydrodynamics is not applicable.
we can explain the elliptic flow from low to high pT in terms of the same physical picture, which is a viscous hydro regime at early stage and a transport regime at late stage.

a transport approach is able to describe anisotropic flow in a wide range of transverse momenta, from the low pT region where the hydro regime is expected to be valid up to the intermediate region, where hydrodynamics suffers form large uncertainties, and finally to the high pT region, where hydro regime is not valid and the flow vanishes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transport approach provides an unified picture of the elliptic flows in the full pT range, from low pT to high pT, where hydrodynamics and perturbative QCD approaches are expected to be valid.
the hydrodynamical regime is reached at a temperature where the system size is of the order of 1/√(σ/η).
a transport approach is able to reproduce the elliptic flow at RHIC, LHC and in the future at FAIR and NICA.
